It covers 3D modeling techniques, fabric and hardware application, simulation tips, and design adjustments tailored for lingerie production. --- ## Overview of 3D Underwear Production and Model Setup This section explains the industry context of 3D underwear production, limitations in current modeling, and initial model setup in CLO software, including body adjustments for better garment fit. - The underwear industry primarily focuses on the appearance of 3D underwear designs, with limited capability to simulate true shape and fit due to hard 3D models. - Most industry 3D underwear models cannot accurately represent the soft, flexible shapes of real garments. - The tutorial uses a virtual model named Chloe in CLO software, adjusting her body to better fit the lingerie design. - Adjustments include enlarging the chest, creating a more prominent chest-to-lower chest gap, shortening the waist and hind legs to reduce back arch, and refining thigh, knee, calf, and shoulder blade proportions. - These adjustments help create a more realistic and coordinated virtual fit for the lingerie. --- ## Creating and Positioning the Bra Steel Ring This section details the process of creating the bra’s steel ring, including fabric assignment, positioning, and simulation constraints. - The steel ring is extracted from a sample or scanned if a physical ring is available; typical steel ring widths range from 8mm to 1cm. - The fabric for the steel ring uses "Trim Hardware" with a focus on adjusting minimum tension to prevent unwanted stretching. - Positioning the steel ring on the curved line below the chest is challenging due to the hard nature of the 3D model's chest. - The steel ring board is fixed onto the model using “fixed needles” and “positioning balls” to ensure even, smooth fitting along the chest curve. - Adjustments to the steel ring shape consider asymmetry (e.g., one side lower than the other) to match the intended design. - The steel ring is shaped first as a core technique to ensure a full, accurate bra cup shape. - The process includes creating curves to shape the cup, adding lines for cutting backlight fabric, and simulating the steel ring’s surface smoothness. --- ## Designing and Adjusting the Backlight Fabric This section covers drawing, applying, and modifying backlight fabric panels, including fabric physical properties and simulation settings. - Backlight fabric is drawn on the model using 3D and 2D drawing tools, with inner lines added for sewing shoulder straps. - Fabric physical properties are crucial: initial use of "Trim Hardware" resulted in a rigid appearance, so the fabric was switched to a default fabric with increased backlight bending strength (from 38 to 60) to balance hardness and smoothness. - The fabric is copied symmetrically, leveled using world coordinates, and arranged carefully to avoid distortion.
